name: Mercury-contact electromagnetic rotation
summary: In 1821 Faraday made a current-carrying wire, dipped in mercury, circle continuously around a magnet pole, turning electric current into continuous motion; Paris experimenters repeated it within weeks.
description: A battery-fed wire maintains contact through mercury while moving continuously around a magnetic pole; the following day’s arrangement improves wire and magnet support.
tier_reason: A major reusable result, process or system within its field; broader multi-field or multi-generation dependence on this exact referent is not established.
why: Following Ørsted's 1820 discovery, Faraday was reviewing the new electromagnetism and tested whether the circular force around a current could produce continuous rotation.

date.basis: Diary entries for 3 and 4 September 1821 quoted by the Royal Institution.

events.statement: A battery-fed wire maintains contact through mercury while moving continuously around a magnetic pole; the following day’s arrangement improves wire and magnet support.
events.caveats: No claim of commercial usefulness or universal invention priority. The surviving 1822 object must not be used as an unqualified 1821 artifact.

evidence.locator: Opening narrative and diary entries for 3–4 September 1821
evidence.supports: Dates the rotating-wire demonstration and describes mercury contact and battery.
The surviving collection object is 1822, distinct from the 1821 demonstration.

events.statement: The Société Philomatique repeated Faraday’s wire-around-magnet experiment on 24 November 1821; Hachette separately acknowledged receiving an instrument from Faraday.
events.scope: Faraday’s wire rotating continuously around a magnet; the Paris repeat of the experiment is documented, but the instrument used and every contact detail are not identified.
events.caveats: The letter does not unambiguously say the instrument Faraday sent was the instrument used in the repetition; mercury and exact mounting of the Paris apparatus are not independently specified.

evidence.supports: Contemporary letter separately reports the 24 November Paris repetition and Faraday’s gift of an instrument; it does not establish that the gifted instrument was used.
